
Reviewed Grok social signals and arXiv papers. The arXiv papers are all too academic/generic with no Claude-specific practical tips. From the Grok signals, Simon Willison's hands-on Haiku workflow post stands out as the strongest candidate — it's grounded in real usage, covers non-obvious productivity patterns (data extraction, SQL generation, speed optimization), and is broadly applicable. The Prompt Engineering Guide for Haiku also offers curated, actionable techniques. The Computer Use docs link is already covered by existing README entries. Claude 3.5 Haiku release post is more of an announcement. Vertex AI post is enterprise/deployment-specific and narrower audience.

## Suggestions

- [Trying out Claude 3.5 Haiku — Speed-Optimized Workflow Patterns](https://simonwillison.net/2024/Oct/24/claude-35-haiku/) — Simon Willison's hands-on real-world tests of Claude 3.5 Haiku for data extraction, SQL generation, and Datasette integration — with concrete prompting patterns and observed speed/cost tradeoffs for high-volume tasks.
